The main takeaway from our work is that

, in contrast to the common belief that plasmon coupling leads to a significant change of the far-field angular distribution of the radiation, in our experiment we do not observe any significant change in the angular distribution.
, while the far-field angular distribution is determined by the dipole moment of the scatterers, the spectral response is determined by the local density of surface plasmon states.

, in the case of plasmon-coulpled nanohole arrays, the far-field angular distribution of the scattered light is independent of the excitation wavelength, which is a direct consequence of the fact that the far-field radiation from the array is a superposition of dipolar fields.
